column1: # OWASP ZAP Baseline Scan — Custom Alert Rules
# This file lets you tune how ZAP classifies individual passive-scan alerts
# for the Banking Platform microservices.
# HOW TO USE
# 1. Edit the action column for any alert ID you want to change.
# 2. Add the -c flag to the docker run command in pipelines/Jenkinsfile:
#      docker run --rm \
#          --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
#          -v "$(pwd)/zap-reports:/zap/wrk:rw" \
#          -v "$(pwd)/security/zap-rules.tsv:/zap/wrk/zap-rules.tsv:ro" \
#          ghcr.io/zaproxy/zaproxy:stable \
#          zap-baseline.py \
#              -t http://host.docker.internal:8081 \
#              -r zap-report.html \
#              -c zap-rules.tsv \
#              -l WARN \
# FORMAT (tab-separated)
#   <alertId>   <action>   # optional comment
# ACTIONS
#   IGNORE  — Suppress the alert entirely (use for confirmed false positives).
#   WARN    — Log the alert in the report but do not affect the pipeline exit code.
#   FAIL    — Cause zap-baseline.py to exit with code 2, marking the Jenkins
#             build UNSTABLE.  Use this for findings you must fix before release.
# FINDING ALERT IDs
#   Run the scan once without this file, then look up numeric IDs in the
#   generated HTML report or at https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/alerts/
# ── Section 1: IGNORE — Suppress informational / false-positive alerts ────────
# These alerts fire frequently on REST APIs and carry little practical risk
# in a local development environment.  Suppressing them reduces noise so
# the team can focus on genuine findings.

column3: # Incomplete or No Cache-Control Header — common for JSON REST responses
# Information Disclosure: Suspicious Comments — dev-time TODO comments
# Non-Storable Content — expected for dynamic API responses
# Retrieved from Cache — informational, not a security issue
# Modern Web Application fingerprint — informational only
# Authentication Request Identified — informational
# Session Management Response Identified — informational
# Verification Request Identified — informational

column1: # ── Section 2: WARN — Review but do not block the build ───────────────────────
# These findings represent security hardening opportunities that should be
# tracked and addressed before moving to production, but are acceptable
# during local development and feature-branch testing.

column3: # Cookie No HttpOnly Flag — set HttpOnly on all session cookies
# Cookie Without Secure Flag — acceptable on plain HTTP locally; fix for HTTPS
# Web Browser XSS Protection Not Enabled — add X-XSS-Protection header
# Cross-Domain JavaScript Source File Inclusion
# Content-Type Header Missing — always set Content-Type in responses
# X-Frame-Options Header Not Set — prevent clickjacking; add DENY or SAMEORIGIN
# X-Content-Type-Options Header Missing — add nosniff to all responses
# Strict-Transport-Security Not Set — expected on plain HTTP; required for HTTPS
# Server Version Leakage via Server Header — remove or obfuscate server banner
# X-Powered-By Header Leaks Technology — remove this header in production
# Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set — add CSP for browser clients
# Cookie Without SameSite Attribute — set SameSite=Lax or Strict
# Permissions-Policy Header Not Set — restrict browser feature access
# Base64 Disclosure — ensure no sensitive data is base64-encoded in responses
# Timestamp Disclosure — review whether timestamps expose internal details
# Cross-Domain Misconfiguration — review CORS configuration
# Reverse Tabnabbing — use rel="noopener noreferrer" on external links

column1: # ── Section 3: FAIL — Serious findings that must be fixed before release ───────
# These alerts indicate meaningful security weaknesses in a banking API.
# The pipeline will be marked UNSTABLE when any of these are detected.
# Open the HTML report, apply the recommended fix, and re-run the pipeline.

column3: # Information Disclosure: Debug Error Messages — never expose stack traces
# Source Code Disclosure via /WEB-INF — misconfigured servlet container
# X-ChromeLogger-Data Header — server-side data leaking via response headers
# X-Debug-Token Header — Spring/framework debug mode active in running app
# PII Disclosure — personally identifiable information in HTTP responses
# Backup File Disclosed — backup/temp files (.bak, ~, .swp) publicly accessible
# Weak Authentication Method — basic auth over plain HTTP; use token-based auth
# Httpoxy — Proxy header misuse leading to server-side request forgery
